title: Add up 13 numbers in how many reads?
hook: Running totals are quick to read but slow to change. One bit trick makes both quick.

doesNotKnow: that x & -x gives a hop that makes prefix sums and updates both take about log n cells

misconception: A running prefix-sum table is cheap to read, so changing one value only needs one cell touched.
objective: The learner can explain that a Fenwick cell i covers the last (i & -i) numbers up to i, so a prefix sum hops down by the lowest 1 bit (13 -> 12 -> 8: 3 reads for 13 numbers) and an update hops up by it (1, 2, 4, 8, 16: 5 cells), both about log2 n.

claims.text: Cell i of a Fenwick tree holds the sum of the last (i & -i) numbers up to position i, that is positions i - (i & -i) + 1 to i; i & -i is the lowest 1 bit of i.
claims.source: Fenwick (1994), 'A new data structure for cumulative frequency tables', Software: Practice and Experience 24(3) (citation from the brief: check before verifying). i & -i isolates the lowest set bit in two's complement (derivation: -i = ~i + 1). · Fact-check pass 21 2026-10-14: VERIFIED: Demo CELL[i] = sum V[i-low(i)+1..i] with low(i) = i & -i; -i = ~i + 1 isolates the lowest set bit. Fenwick 1994, Softw. Pract. Exp. 24(3):327-336 (DOI 10.1002/spe.4380240306) confirmed bibliographically by web search; paper not opened (host blocked). Definition verified against the code and derivation.

claims.text: To add up the first 13 numbers you read cells 13, 12 and 8 (1101, 1100, 1000): each hop clears one 1 bit, and their ranges 13, 9-12 and 1-8 tile 1-13 with no gaps.
claims.source: Demo.tsx hopsDown(13); builder re-ran in Node (2026-10-14): [13..13], [9..12], [1..8]; 13 = 1101, 12 = 1100, 8 = 1000. v2: the stage keeps the trail 13=1101 -> 12=1100 -> 8=1000 -> 0=0000 and the reveal reads the recorded run. Prefix 15 reads 15, 14, 12, 8 (4 cells); prefix 7 reads 7, 6, 4. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 24): VERIFIED. Own node hopsDown(13) = 13, 12, 8 (1101, 1100, 1000); ranges 13, 9-12, 1-8 tile 1-13; sum 61 = RUN[13]. Prefix 15: 15, 14, 12, 8; prefix 7: 7, 6, 4. Reveal requires milestone tiled (start 13), so qSum exists.

claims.text: On the stage numbers (3 1 4 1 5 9 2 6 5 3 5 8 9 7 9 3) cells 13, 12 and 8 hold 9, 21 and 31, which add to 61, the sum of the first 13 numbers.
claims.source: Builder's Node run, 2026-10-14 (cells 1..16: 3 4 4 9 5 14 2 31 5 8 5 21 9 16 9 80; prefix 13 directly = 61). The numbers are fixed digits of pi, chosen for display only. · Fact-check pass 21 2026-10-14: VERIFIED: node: cells 1..16 = 3 4 4 9 5 14 2 31 5 8 5 21 9 16 9 80; 9 + 21 + 31 = 61 = direct prefix sum. The digits are those of pi (3.141592653589793).

claims.text: Changing position 1 hops up 1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 8 -> 16: 5 Fenwick cells change, while a plain running-total row changes all 16 entries.
claims.source: Demo.tsx hopsUp(1); builder re-ran in Node: [1, 2, 4, 8, 16]. Running-total row: every prefix total 1..16 includes position 1 (derivation). v2 draws both on stage after 'Change position 1' (milestone update). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 24): VERIFIED. Own node hopsUp(1) = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 (5 cells); every running total 1..16 includes position 1, so all 16 change. Stage readouts 5 and 16 match.

claims.text: Both directions take about log2 n hops, not n.
claims.source: Down: i - lowbit(i) removes exactly one set bit, so at most popcount(i) <= floor(log2 n) + 1 hops. Up: i + lowbit(i) has a strictly higher lowest set bit, so at most floor(log2 n) + 1 hops within n. Here n = 16: at most 5 hops (the update from 1 takes exactly 5). Derivation; Fenwick (1994) cited from the brief, not opened, and the sentence does not depend on it. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 24): VERIFIED. Re-derived: down hops = popcount(i), up hops <= floor(log2 n) + 1. Own node over i = 1..16: max 4 down, max 5 up (from 1). 'About log2 n' accurate. Fenwick 1994 not opened; not needed.

claims.text: The stage's Σ row holds the plain running totals of the 16 numbers: 3, 4, 8, 9, 14, 23, 25, 31, 36, 39, 44, 52, 61, 68, 77, 80.
claims.source: Demo.tsx RUN = prefix sums of V (3 1 4 1 5 9 2 6 5 3 5 8 9 7 9 3); builder's Node run, 2026-10-14. Entry 13 = 61 matches c3. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 24): VERIFIED. Own node prefix sums of V = 3 1 4 1 5 9 2 6 5 3 5 8 9 7 9 3: 3, 4, 8, 9, 14, 23, 25, 31, 36, 39, 44, 52, 61, 68, 77, 80.

recall.question: In a Fenwick tree, the prefix sum up to position 22 (binary 10110) reads how many cells?
recall.why: One cell per 1 bit: 22 -> 20 -> 16 -> 0, reading cells 22, 20 and 16.
